extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates studying commutative algebra / ring theory
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, definitions and propositions about primary decomposition, associated primes, saturations S(a), localization behavior, and related constructions (constructible topology, polynomial extension, colon ideals) in commutative rings and modules. Includes uniqueness theorems, existence constructions (including transfinite induction), and many useful lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructible topology XC: compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected
rubrics_metrics.description: XC (X with constructible topology) is compact Hausdorff; furthermore it is totally disconnected (every connected component is a singleton).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: closed sets in XC are finite unions of arbitrary intersections of clopen subbasic sets, 1_X: XC → X is a continuous bijection and if A/R is absolutely flat then X is Hausdorff, so a continuous bijection from compact domain to Hausdorff codomain is a homeomorphism. For total disconnectedness: for any p ≠ q there exists a clopen X_f separating them, so connected components are singletons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological criterion: continuous bijection from compact domain to Hausdorff codomain is a homeomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuous bijection from a compact domain to a Hausdorff codomain is a homeomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly: e.g. 1_X: XC → X is a homeomorphism when domain is compact and codomain Hausdorff (arises when A/R is absolutely flat).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — isolated set of prime ideals belonging to a
rubrics_metrics.description: Σ is an isolated set of prime ideals belonging to a if whenever p' is a prime ideal belonging to a and p' ⊆ p for some p ∈ Σ then p' ∈ Σ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition isolates a subset of associated primes that are minimal with respect to containment relative to a; used to state independence of certain intersections in decompositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.10 (2nd uniqueness theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a be a decomposable ideal with minimal primary decomposition a = ⋂_{i=1}^n q_i, and let {p_{i1},…,p_{im}} be an isolated set of prime ideals of a. Then q_{i1} ∩ … ∩ q_{im} is independent of the decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the multiplicative set S = A − (p_{i1} ∪ … ∪ p_{im}), uniqueness of S(a) as contraction of S^{-1}a, and Proposition 4.9 to identify the corresponding contracted intersection. This yields uniqueness of intersections corresponding to isolated prime subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary — isolated primary components are uniquely determined
rubrics_metrics.description: The isolated primary components (the q_i corresponding to minimal prime ideals p_i) are uniquely determined by a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special case of Theorem 4.10 for a singleton minimal prime set Σ = {p}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — saturation S(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a multiplicatively closed set S and canonical map φ_S: A → S^{-1}A, define S(a) as the contraction along φ_S of S^{-1}a (called the saturation of a w.r.t S). Equivalently S(a) = {x ∈ A : ∃ s ∈ S such that s x ∈ a} = a^e c ⊇ a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This equality is used repeatedly; the equivalence is by interpreting x/1 ∈ a^e in localization and translating back to existence of s with s x ∈ a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.12(2): S(0) = ker(φ_S)
rubrics_metrics.description: The saturation of the zero ideal is the kernel of the localization map φ_S: A → S^{-1}A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because (0)^e = (0) and contraction of the zero ideal from localization is precisely elements sent to 0 in S^{-1}A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.12(3): localization preserves p-primary for Sp
rubrics_metrics.description: Let S_p = A  ackslash p for p prime. If q is p-primary then S_p(q) = q (saturation with respect to S_p leaves a p-primary ideal unchanged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied via Proposition 4.9: if S does not meet the radical p then contraction after localization returns the same ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.12(4): Sp(0) is contained in every p-primary ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: For S_p = A  ackslash p, every element of S_p(0) lies in every p-primary ideal of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: x ∈ S_p(0) means x/1 = 0/1 so s x = 0 for some s ∈ S_p; since s ∉ p, sx = 0 ∈ q for any p-primary q, forcing x ∈ q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.12(5): monotonicity in multiplicative sets
rubrics_metrics.description: If S1 ⊆ S2 are multiplicative subsets then S1(a) ⊆ S2(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from the definition: any s ∈ S1 is also in S2 so elements witnessing membership for S1(a) also witness membership for S2(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.12(6): monotonicity in ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: If b is an ideal containing a then S(a) ⊆ S(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of extension/contraction preserving inclusion: a ⊆ b ⇒ a^e ⊆ b^e ⇒ a^{ec} ⊆ b^{ec}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXII: extension and contraction preserve inclusion order
rubrics_metrics.description: Both extension (to S^{-1}A or similar) and contraction preserve order of inclusion of ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension: generators of b^e include generators of a^e; Contraction: preimage under ring map preserves inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness of associated/minimal primes for decomposable ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a has a minimal primary decomposition a = ⋂_{i=1}^n q_i then the set of associated primes {p_i = r(q_i)} is finite; equivalently Spec(A/a) has finitely many irreducible components corresponding to these minimal primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses correspondence between irreducible components of Spec(A/a) and minimal primes of A/a and Proposition 4.6 identifying minimal primes with minimal associated primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: In absolutely flat rings, primary ideals are maximal
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is absolutely flat and q is a primary ideal of A, then A/q is absolutely flat and local, hence a field, so q is maximal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: in absolutely flat rings every nonunit is a zero divisor; in A/q every element is either unit or nilpotent, so A/q is a local absolutely flat ring hence a field.

rubrics_metrics.name: C(X) behaviour: primary ideals lie in unique maximal ideal and (0) not decomposable for infinite X
rubrics_metrics.description: In C(X) (continuous real-valued functions on a compact Hausdorff X), maximal ideals are m_x = {f : f(x)=0}; every primary ideal is contained in a unique maximal ideal; if X is infinite then (0) cannot be decomposable (there are infinitely many minimal primes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Urysohn's lemma to show that a primary ideal contained in two different m_x and m_y would force contradiction; infinite X gives infinitely many maximal ideals, contradicting finiteness required for decomposability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial extension properties: a[x], p[x], q[x], and decomposition preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: For ideal a ⊆ A, the extension a^e in A[x] equals a[x]; if p is prime then p[x] is prime in A[x]; if q is p-primary then q[x] is p[x]-primary and r(q[x]) = p[x]; primary decompositions extend via a[x] = ⋂ q_i[x] and minimality is preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use coefficient-wise reduction modulo primes and the fact that A[x]/p[x] ≅ (A/p)[x] is an integral domain; nilpotence of coefficients gives nilpotence of polynomials, and radicals behave termwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of zero divisors via minimal primes D(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: x is a zero divisor iff x lies in some minimal prime p containing a suitable annihilator (equivalently ∃ a ≠ 0 with x ∈ (0:a)). Thus zero divisors correspond to elements lying in primes in D(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: given x zero divisor, pick a with x a = 0 and consider minimal prime in A/(0:a) and lift back; conversely use maximal multiplicative sets to show containment in some minimal prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves annihilators: Ann(x)^e = Ann(x/1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For canonical map φ: A → S^{-1}A, Ann(x)^e = S^{-1}Ann(x) = Ann(x/1) (and Ann(x/s) = Ann(x/1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a/t in the extended annihilator, translate equations in localization back to existence of q ∈ S with axq = 0; conversely obvious direction holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes under localization: D(S^{-1}A) = D(A) ∩ Spec(S^{-1}A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimal associated primes of 0 in the localization S^{-1}A correspond to minimal primes of A containing (0:a) that survive localization: D(S^{-1}A) = D(A) ∩ Spec(S^{-1}A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved via correspondence of primes under localization (Proposition 3.11) and minimality arguments using annihilators and contraction/extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 11: Sp(0) is p-primary and smallest p-primary; decomposition of 0 via Sp(0)
rubrics_metrics.description: For p ∈ D(A), Sp(0) is p-primary and is the smallest p-primary ideal. Moreover 0 = ⋂_{p ∈ min(A)} Sp(0), and if every associated prime is isolated then this yields a minimal primary decomposition of 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show Sp(0) is primary using powers and radicals; use minimal primes min(A) to express nilradical and obtain decomposition; removing superfluous components yields Ass(0) ⊆ min(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXIII: p(n) is smallest p-primary ideal containing p^n
rubrics_metrics.description: For prime p and integer n, p^{(n)} := S_p(p^n) (saturation) is the smallest p-primary ideal containing p^n; in particular p^{(n)} equals the p-primary component arising from a minimal primary decomposition of p^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show any p-primary ideal containing p^n must contain p^{(n)} by localization argument; minimal primary decomposition expresses p^{(n)} as the corresponding qi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXIV: p(m+n) is smallest p-primary containing p(m)p(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: p^{(m+n)} is the smallest p-primary ideal containing p^{(m)} p^{(n)}. If p^{(m)} p^{(n)} has a minimal primary decomposition, then p^{(m+n)} is the p-primary component of that product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses localization Sp and minimality-of-radical reasoning; uses that r(p^{(m)} p^{(n)}) = p and uniqueness of isolated prime component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim XXV: colon test for radical of p-primary q
rubrics_metrics.description: If q is p-primary and (q : x) is maximal among ideals of the form (q : y) for y ∉ q, then r(q) = (q : x) (i.e., the radical equals that maximal colon ideal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses repeated application of colon identities and maximality to deduce containment relations leading to (q:x) = r(q) = p; used to extract prime components via colon ideals in decompositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: S_f(a) description and computation via isolated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: For f ∈ A, S_f(a) = {x ∈ A : f^n x ∈ a for some n > 0} = ⋃_{n>0} (a : f^n). If a = ⋂_{i=1}^n q_i and Σ is the set of minimal primes containing f (equivalently those p_i with f ∈ p_i), then S_f(a) = ⋂_{i∈I} q_i where I indexes primes not meeting S_f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One checks which primary components survive when localizing at the multiplicative set generated by f; uses existence of exponents n_i to clear membership in appropriate qi and pigeonhole argument to choose uniform n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of primary decomposition via transfinite induction
rubrics_metrics.description: Any ideal a is decomposable: using Zorn's lemma and iterative construction (possibly transfinite), one can build a (possibly infinite) intersection a = ⋂_{γ<β} q_γ of primary ideals; the process terminates by cardinality bounds on chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct minimal primes successively: choose minimal prime p_1 over a, let q_1 = S_{p_1}(a) etc., form maximal a_2 containing a but intersecting correctly, iterate successor and limit ordinal steps; termination occurs at ordinal ≤ |A|.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 4.3*: intersection of p-primary submodules is p-primary
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q_i (i=1..n) are p-primary submodules of a module M then Q = ⋂_{i=1}^n Q_i is p-primary; r((Q:M)) = p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zero divisors on M/Q are nilpotent because nilpotency holds on each M/Q_i; use (⋂ Q_i : M) = ⋂ (Q_i : M) and radicals to show radical equals p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.4*: colon behaviour for p-primary submodule Q ⊆ M
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If x ∈ Q then (Q : x) = (1). (b) If x ∉ Q then (Q : x) is p-primary and r(Q : x) = p. (c) If x ∉ p then (Q : x) = Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are module-theoretic analogues of primary ideal properties: colon ideals either become whole module, remain primary with same radical, or equal Q when x avoids the radical p.
